name: Chainlink
description: Oracle network. Agents read Chainlink Data Feeds (AggregatorV3 proxy contracts, e.g. ETH/USD) on-chain for reference prices, and move tokens or messages between chains with CCIP by calling the CCIP Router (getFee, then ccipSend). LINK is the network's ERC-677 token and a CCIP fee token.

keyFunctions.description: Returns (uint80 roundId, int256 answer, uint256 startedAt, uint256 updatedAt, uint80 answeredInRound). answer is the ETH / USD price scaled by 10^decimals() (8 here). Heartbeat for this feed is 3600 s and deviation threshold 0.5% (per Chainlink's feed directory): the answer updates when price moves more than 0.5% or 3600 s pass. Reject the answer if block.timestamp - updatedAt > heartbeat (plus a small buffer), if answer <= 0, or if updatedAt == 0.
Number of decimals in answer (8 for this feed). Always read it rather than hard-coding; some Chainlink feeds use 18.
Human-readable pair, returns "ETH / USD". Use it to sanity-check you have the right proxy.
Same tuple as latestRoundData for a historical roundId (round ids are phase-encoded; not guaranteed contiguous across aggregator upgrades).
Current underlying aggregator behind this proxy. Always read prices from the proxy, never the aggregator, since Chainlink swaps aggregators behind the proxy.
Aggregator interface version.

Send a cross-chain message and/or tokens. Args: destinationChainSelector (uint64, NOT the EVM chainId; see CCIP Directory), Client.EVM2AnyMessage {bytes receiver = abi.encode(receiverAddress) for EVM destinations; bytes data (payload, empty for token-only transfers); EVMTokenAmount[] tokenAmounts {address token, uint256 amount} (tokens must be CCIP-enabled on this lane and approved to this Router first); address feeToken (address(0) = pay in native gas token via msg.value, or LINK / listed fee token, approved to the Router); bytes extraArgs}. extraArgs = bytes4 tag 0x181dcf10 (GENERIC_EXTRA_ARGS_V2_TAG) + abi.encode(uint256 gasLimit, bool allowOutOfOrderExecution); use gasLimit 0 for token-only transfers to an EOA; empty extraArgs defaults to 200k gas but Chainlink recommends always setting it explicitly. Returns bytes32 messageId. If paying natively, msg.value must be >= getFee(); overpayment is not refunded.

Fee for the exact same (destinationChainSelector, message) you will pass to ccipSend, denominated in message.feeToken (native wei if feeToken = address(0)). Call right before sending; add a small buffer when paying natively.
True if the destination chain selector has a lane from this chain. Check before ccipSend (otherwise UnsupportedDestinationChain).
Wrapped native token accepted as a fee token on this chain (WETH 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2).
OnRamp contract for a destination selector (zero address if no lane).
Returns "Router 1.2.0".
Send LINK (18 decimals).
Approve a spender, e.g. the CCIP Router when paying CCIP fees in LINK.

contracts.name: Chainlink L2 Sequencer Uptime Status Feed

keyFunctions.description: answer 0 = sequencer up, 1 = sequencer down. startedAt = when the status last changed. offchainApis.name: Data Feeds directory (data.chain.link)
offchainApis.use: Search every Chainlink feed by pair and network; each feed page shows the proxy address to call, decimals, heartbeat and deviation threshold, and whether it is deprecated.

offchainApis.name: Feed reference data directory (JSON)
offchainApis.use: Machine-readable list of all feeds for one network (the same data docs.chain.link renders). Fields: name, proxyAddress (call this), decimals, heartbeat, threshold, feedCategory, docs.hidden / shutdownDate. {network} examples: mainnet (Ethereum), ethereum-mainnet-base-1, ethereum-mainnet-arbitrum-1, ethereum-mainnet-optimism-1, matic-mainnet, bsc-mainnet, avalanche-mainnet. Some entries have secondaryProxyAddress/secondaryProxyEns (e.g. Base ETH/USD): the standard proxy is the one whose ens is the plain pair name (eth-usd); 'svr' proxies are Smart Value Recapture variants.

offchainApis.name: CCIP Directory
offchainApis.use: Per-chain Router address, chain selector, fee tokens, supported lanes and supported tokens (with token pool and rate limits) for CCIP mainnet.

offchainApis.name: CCIP Explorer
offchainApis.use: Track a CCIP message by messageId or source tx hash (status: waiting for finality, committed, success/failure; manual execution if it failed on the destination).

actions.name: read-price
actions.description: Get a reference USD price on-chain
actions.how: Call latestRoundData() on the feed proxy for the pair and chain (this file for ETH/BTC/USDC; any other pair: look up the proxyAddress on data.chain.link or the reference-data-directory JSON). price = answer / 10^decimals(). Reject if answer <= 0 or now - updatedAt > heartbeat. On Arbitrum/Base/Optimism first check the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed (answer == 0 and now - startedAt > grace period).

actions.name: ccip-token-transfer
actions.description: Bridge a CCIP-supported token to another chain
actions.how: 1) Confirm the token is supported on the lane in the CCIP Directory and router.isChainSupported(destSelector). 2) token.approve(router, amount). 3) Build EVM2AnyMessage{receiver: abi.encode(recipient), data: "", tokenAmounts: [(token, amount)], feeToken: LINK or address(0), extraArgs: 0x181dcf10 ++ abi.encode(0, true)}. 4) fee = router.getFee(destSelector, msg). 5) If feeToken is LINK, LINK.approve(router, fee) (plus amount if LINK is also the token sent); else send value = fee. 6) router.ccipSend(destSelector, msg). 7) Track messageId on ccip.chain.link.

actions.name: ccip-message
actions.description: Send arbitrary data to a receiver contract on another chain
actions.how: Same as token transfer with data = your payload, tokenAmounts = [], and extraArgs gasLimit sized for the receiver's ccipReceive (the receiver must implement CCIPReceiver / IAny2EVMMessageReceiver).

actions.name: get-link
actions.how: Use the LINK address for the chain from this file (from docs.chain.link/resources/link-token-contracts). On BNB Chain and Polygon, bridged LINK from the chain's native bridge is not ERC-677 and must be converted with Chainlink PegSwap before use with Chainlink services.

risks: Stale prices: a feed only updates on its deviation threshold or heartbeat; always compare updatedAt with the heartbeat listed for that feed, and do not assume the same heartbeat across chains (e.g. ETH/USD is 3600 s on Ethereum but 27 s on Polygon, 86400 s on Avalanche).

Feeds get deprecated: Chainlink marks feeds for shutdown on data.chain.link and in the directory JSON (shutdownDate / hidden). A deprecated proxy can stop updating; check before integrating and re-check periodically.

Use the proxy, never the aggregator address; aggregators are replaced during upgrades. Several networks also list SVR (Smart Value Recapture) proxies and Arbitrum lists hidden 'cre-backup' proxies for the same pair with different decimals (18): read decimals() and use the standard proxy unless you specifically want SVR.

L2s (Arbitrum, Base, Optimism): if the sequencer is down, feeds can look fresh but be wrong for users who cannot transact; check the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed and enforce a grace period after it comes back up. The directory JSON currently flags the Optimism sequencer feed as hidden although the L2 sequencer docs page still lists it.

Data feeds are market references with a deviation band (e.g. 0.5%); they are not exact execution prices and can be manipulated on low-liquidity assets ('medium'/'high' risk categories on data.chain.link).

CCIP fees: getFee depends on the destination, data size, gas limit and token amounts; overpaid native fees are not refunded. Messages wait for source-chain finality (minutes on Ethereum, can be longer on some chains).

CCIP rate limits: each token pool has per-lane capacity and refill-rate limits; transfers above the available capacity revert. Check the token's rate limits in the CCIP Directory before large transfers.

CCIP chain selectors are not EVM chain IDs; sending to a wrong selector or an unsupported lane reverts with UnsupportedDestinationChain. Receiver must be abi.encode(address) for EVM destinations; tokens sent to a contract that cannot handle them may be stuck.
Bridged LINK from BNB Chain's and Polygon's native bridges is not ERC-677 and is not usable with Chainlink services; use PegSwap to convert. LINK on Avalanche reports symbol LINK.e.
notes: DefiLlama lists Chainlink as a parent protocol 'chainlink' with child entries (Chainlink Requests 'chainlink-requests', CCIP, Chainlink Staking); 'chainlink' is used because this file covers Data Feeds, CCIP and LINK together. Feed proxies are the standard (non-SVR) proxies from Chainlink's reference data directory JSON, which docs.chain.link/data-feeds/price-feeds/addresses loads; on Base the standard eth-usd and btc-usd proxies appear as secondaryProxyAddress of the shared-SVR entries. LINK/USD is included for Ethereum only. All feeds were checked on 2026-11-25 with description(), decimals() (all 8) and latestRoundData() (ETH ~1652 USD, BTC ~58,950 USD, USDC ~0.9999 USD); all CCIP routers returned typeAndVersion 'Router 1.2.0' and isChainSupported true for the other test chains; all LINK addresses returned decimals 18. Left out: the Ethereum Feed Registry: docs.chain.link/data-feeds/feed-registry now redirects to the Data Feeds overview and no current official page lists its address, so it is omitted (read individual proxies instead). Other CCIP contracts per chain (RMN proxy/armProxy, TokenAdminRegistry, RegistryModuleOwnerCustom, TokenPoolFactory, OnRamps/OffRamps) are listed in the CCIP Directory and in https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation/blob/main/src/config/data/ccip/v1_2_0/mainnet/chains.json. Every other price feed (thousands, on 50+ networks) is listed at data.chain.link with its proxy address. Polygon here means Polygon PoS (chainId 137).
